qualification: Published v0.4.11 -> v0.4.12 Docker evaluation upgrade with both releases' published bundles, images and launchers, on one Linux arm64 Docker engine, from a fresh v0.4.11 installation (portable lineage 0011-0021). Both releases require head 0021, so the pair runs no migration: no transition opens and the writer drain does not run. It exercises v0.4.12's read-only check after a failure in migrating (ADR-0156 amendment 2). Logical backup on the same host. Not the published lineage, not off-host recovery, not Kubernetes.

outcome.no_pending_migration_with_writers_connec: passed: v0.4.12 migrate reported 0021 -> 0021 in 0.3 s and refreshed only the stamp's updated_at
outcome.installed_release_against_upgraded_datab: observed: v0.4.11's gateway and worker, run in v0.4.12's prepared graph, accepted the upgraded database's authority and reported healthy; v0.4.11's read-only check passed, and its migrate changed only updated_at
outcome.interrupted_stamp: passed: over a hand-set 0019..0021 marker and the 0021 ledger, v0.4.12's gateway and worker refused at their epoch stage and its read-only check exited 1; v0.4.12 migrate returned the marker to 0021 and changed nothing else but updated_at
outcome.upgrade_with_injections: passed: with the migration boundary lock held, migrate refused after 60 s (55P03) without writes, the launcher's read-only check passed and it directed a rerun with no migration open; over a hand-set 0019..0021 marker with the same lock held, migrate refused, the check refused and the launcher kept the restore alternative; the same command then completed
outcome.rollback_by_restore: passed once with the v0.4.11 bundle: the pristine pre-upgrade set, matching apart from updated_at and the known flattened constraint text
outcome.launcher_direction: v0.4.12's message after a failure in migrating followed its read-only check: first drill of the passing branch from published bundles; the refusing branch was reached only on a hand-set state
outcome.completion_message: finding: after each completed upgrade the launcher said the installed release cannot serve the upgraded database; for this pair, which runs no migration, v0.4.11 accepted it. Its message after a failure in migrated says the installed release refuses the database; that this is wrong too is inferred, because no migrated failure was injected

digest_method: snapshot.py: one REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY transaction as the bundled superuser over the local socket, hashing every row of every table (with the pre-upgrade column list, so added columns leave existing rows' digests unchanged), the SQLx ledger, schema_metadata, public views, extensions, each tenant's audit chain and audit prefix, and the catalogue: every public constraint and index definition, column definition, trigger, row-level security policy, function (definition digest, owner, SECURITY DEFINER, settings and ACL) and relation (kind, owner, ACL and row-level security flags). expected.py checks a comparison's catalogue change against the object names each migration creates or replaces, listed by hand from its SQL; it checks names, not definitions. A comparison block leaves out tables_added when none were added, catalogue when it is identical, and catalogue_expected when no migration was expected

upgrade_with_injections.resume_path: a resume at migrating reruns up postgres and both bootstraps, then migrate; after a migrate failure the v0.4.12 launcher runs the read-only check and words its message by the result

deviations: The first v0.4.11 up refused preparation with 'generate-secrets: secret parent directory metadata was refused' before any evaluation service had started: Alpine's adduser had created the drill HOME with the setgid bit (2755), so the launcher's state directories were 2700, and generate-secrets requires exactly 700. The partial .synveda state was removed, HOME was made 0755 without setgid, and up was rerun from scratch. The v0.4.7 -> v0.4.8 drill hit the same setup mistake. This is a drill-host artifact, and the launcher refused correctly. It is from the operator's session; install.log holds only the rerun.

The trailing stamp in interrupted_stamp and the open transition in attempt 2 were set by hand (UPDATE public.schema_metadata SET migration_head = '0019..0021'), because this pair never opens a transition.
v0.4.11 was probed in v0.4.12's prepared graph with its own product image, not under its own up, and no request was sent through its gateway.
expected.py exited 1 for the restore of the pristine set, on the flattened capture_batches_retry_check alone.

Sections of the v0.4.10 -> v0.4.11 record with no counterpart here are left out: clean_upgrade.catalogue_change and new_table_privileges, because no migration ran; installed_launcher_against_open_transition and gateway_against_open_transition, because this pair opens no transition; and incompatible_releases, replaced by installed_release_against_upgraded_database because v0.4.11 accepted the upgraded database instead of refusing it.
